IEA (2025). Can low-temperature heat in factories be electrified competitively? Commentary by Richard Simon and Pol Guardia Calsina, 9 December 2025. IEA, Paris. https://www.iea.org/commentaries/can-low-temperature-heat-in-factories-be-electrified-competitively

Web commentary saved as .mhtml (decoded from the MIME parts; the HTML embeds the Highcharts SVGs but no data tables or data labels). Main file holds only printed values from chart notes: boiler/heat-pump efficiency assumptions (coal 84%, gas 87%, electric 98%, heat pump 350% = COP 3.5), WACC 8-12%, and German hybrid TES sizing (48 MWh/3 MW; 24 MWh/3 MW, water tank) with the optimised gas-boiler utilisation. The regional LCOH bars (USD/MWh, 2024) and German hybrid LCOH (EUR/MWh, 2024) are NOT printed; they were reconstructed from SVG bar geometry and go to other-values as read-from-chart (cross-checked against the text: US e-boiler ~4x gas energy cost, China ~2x; heat-pump capex near gas LCOH in US and coal LCOH in India). Capex per kW and electric-boiler/heat-pump equipment costs are never printed. No page numbers: locators are section headings and chart titles. The parent report Renewables for Industry - Electrification of low-temperature heat and steam (IEA 2025) holds the underlying assumptions and is not held.
